full_judgment: 8. I have considered the plaint. It appears to me that amendment of the plaint sought for as quoted above is quite in conformity with the plaint case and if the same is allowed that would in no way change the nature and character of the suit and the plaint. From the judgments of the courts below it appears that the trial Court gave the finding of possession of the suitland in favour of the plaintiffs, but the appellate Court did not reverse the said finding of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record. The trial Court gave clear finding that though DW 1 Aroz Ali claimed possession of the suit land through their bargadars, namely, Shamsu and Keramat, yet none of the said persons was examined in order to prove their possession in the suit land, Mr Ramjan Ali Khan tried to argue that non examination of the bargadars cannot be a ground to disbelieve other DWs in deciding the factum of possession of the suitland. The submission of Mr Khan cannot be accepted for the simple reason that DW 1 deposed that they possess the suit land through bargadars, therefore, it was incumbent upon them to examine the bargadars. And for non examination of the bargadars an adverse presumption can very much be drawn against the defendants under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act.
